statement: No systematic, actively-maintained, structured (queryable) scholarly database of writing systems with decipherment-status/origin-classification metadata comparable to what this app's data model needs was found. ISO 15924 (maintained with the Unicode Consortium as registration authority, 210+ scripts) is a practical identification/encoding standard for software localization and digital text processing — useful as a script-existence checklist and ID reference, but carries no historical-origin, genealogical-descent, or decipherment-status metadata. Omniglot (founded by Simon Ager, 1998; 2,200+ languages, 365 writing systems) is real and actively maintained but hobbyist-academic, not peer-reviewed. The standard academic reference remains a static print/digital volume: The World's Writing Systems, ed. Peter T. Daniels and William Bright (Oxford University Press, 1996, ~80 signed scholarly articles), not a queryable database. The peer-reviewed journal Writing Systems Research (founded 2009) ceased publication in 2019 — a real, citable gap.

sources.citation: ISO 15924 — Wikipedia; Unicode ISO 15924 Registration Authority.
Daniels, Peter T., and William Bright, eds. The World's Writing Systems. Oxford University Press, 1996.
sources.author: Daniels and Bright

notes: This is itself a documented data gap worth recording, not something to paper over, per this project's standing "Unknown is a valid answer" discipline.
